analysis.title: Global Energy Best Ideas List (November 2, 2026)
key_insights: The RBC Global Energy Best Ideas List returned 8.1% in October, versus 12.7% for the iShares S&P Global Energy ETF (IXC) and 11.5% for the hybrid benchmark (75% IXC, 25% JXI). The list trailed both benchmarks for the month.
YTD total return is 47.0% for the list, versus 54.8% for IXC and 42.8% for the hybrid benchmark. Since inception the list is up 345.4%, versus 101.6% for IXC and 115.5% for the hybrid.
Technip Energies (TE-FP) and Patterson-UTI Energy (PTEN-US) were added this month, both rated Outperform. There were no removals.

Technip Energies: record EUR 12.7bn order intake at 3.5x book-to-bill, with the majority outside the Middle East. FY26 expectations were rebased at 2Q and RBC expects a gradual margin recovery in 2027. It trades at 6.0x FY27E adj. EV/EBITDA, below its five-year average and below Middle East E&C peers. Price target EUR 42.

Patterson-UTI: active rigs are up 16 (+18%) to 104 since the April trough. Drilling Services and Drilling Products EBITDA grew 8% and 57% y/y. RBC expects FCF of $444MM in 2027 (38% FCF/EBITDA conversion) and a 2028 FCF yield of 11% vs 10% for land drilling peers. It trades at 4.8x/4.5x 2027/28E EV/EBITDA vs a historical average of 6.3x. Price target $17.

BP: RBC expects gearing (ex. leases) to fall to 10% at YE2026 from 23% at YE2025, and net debt to reach the $14-18bn target by end 3Q26, well ahead of the end-2027 goal. RBC sees refining as the tightest part of the energy complex, with about 45% of Russian refining capacity reported offline and Middle East outages. It estimates BP's 2026 refining margin at $27/bbl vs $13/bbl in 2025. BP trades at 3.5x 2026E EV/DACF vs 4.4x for the European peer group. Price target GBp 720.

Refined product inventories are well below seasonal averages, with the Strait of Hormuz closed and limited crude flows through it. RBC expects a very tight market absent significant demand destruction.

Suncor: the 2026 Investor Day plan targets $2bn of incremental mid-cycle free funds flow (at US$65 WTI), 100,000 bbl/d of added upstream production, a 10% refinery capacity uplift to 511,000 bbl/d, and a US$5/bbl lower WTI break-even of US$38. Monthly buybacks rise 50% to $750mm from October 2026. Price target C$110.

Canadian Natural Resources: net debt was $14.53bn at June 30, 2026, which supports a 75% distribution of free cash flow to shareholders under its policy (60% at or above $16bn, 100% below $13bn). Price target C$86.

Cheniere: 95% contracted through 2035, liquefaction capacity of about 56 MTPA growing to 60-63 MTPA, with SPL Train 7 fully contracted and CCL Train 4 half contracted. New trains could be built at about 7x Capex/EBITDA. Price target $319, below the $330.32 current price.
Williams (WMB) is positioned for growing power and gas demand through Transco expansions and hyperscaler 'Power Innovation' projects. Targeted leverage is 3.5-4.0x. Price target $87.

Kodiak Gas Services: RBC forecasts a 5-year adj. EBITDA CAGR of about 16% through 2030 and sees a customer agreement for behind-the-meter power as a possible catalyst. The stock is $46.86 vs a $52.97 add price. Price target $82.

Enerflex: power generation backlog is 1.75GW on two large data center awards. RBC sees about 300bps of EBITDA margin expansion over 2025-2027E and the stock trades at 5.3x/4.0x 2027/28E EV/EBITDA. Price target $33.

Tamboran Resources (Outperform, Speculative risk): price target of $55 reflects a 10-15% discount to a risked NAV of $60-65/share. Australian domestic gas is contracted at about US$9/MMBtu and JKM is above US$20/MMBtu vs about $3/Mcf Henry Hub. The stock is $31.14 vs a $37.88 add price.
California Resources: risked NAV of $80-85/share at a 10-15% discount rate, with the first CTV carbon injection achieved. Price target $77.

Woodside: Scarborough was 98% complete at 30 June, with first LNG targeted for late 4Q 2026. Louisiana LNG was 28% complete, with T-1 by 2029. Operating cash flow is projected to grow at more than 6% CAGR through 2032, and RBC expects the 80% dividend payout ratio to hold. Price target A$35.

Northland Power: both offshore wind projects should be fully de-risked by late 2026, with about $550mm EBITDA and $180mm FCF annually on completion. The company plans a development pipeline update with Q3/26 results in November 2026. Price target C$27, vs a $21.65 current price.

EDP Renovaveis: RBC sees US renewables (about 50% of the business) benefiting from higher power prices as deployment slows. Recurring earnings ex-asset rotation grew 4x y/y in 2025, and RBC estimates an extra USD 40m/year of EBITDA from recontracting by 2030 and USD 180m/year by 2035. Price target EUR 17.
Ovintiv is Restricted because RBC is advising Ovintiv on its all-cash acquisition of Logan Energy Corp, announced October 26, 2026. RBC gives no rating or price target.

Pembina and AltaGas: Pembina expects positive FCF after dividends and capex over 2026-2030 and targets over 80% fee-based EBITDA (PT C$77). AltaGas is reducing leverage toward 4.5-5.0x debt/EBITDA after deciding to keep its 10% MVP stake (PT C$59).

PrairieSky: 2026E/27E production is 64%/65% liquids-weighted and RBC forecasts 4%/3% corporate production growth. Mannville Heavy and Clearwater plays are leading activity. RBC forecasts 15-20% y/y growth within the Mannville play at current crude prices. Price target C$42.

market_movers.rationale: Added to the Best Ideas list on a record EUR 12.7bn order intake (3.5x book-to-bill), rebased FY26 estimates and a 6.0x FY27E EV/EBITDA valuation below its five-year average.
Added on rising US drilling activity driving margin expansion, improving FCF conversion and a valuation below its 6.3x historical average.
The Investor Day plan targets $2bn of incremental free funds flow, and monthly buybacks rise 50% to $750mm.
Fast deleveraging, strong refining margins and a lower valuation than European peers.
Improving California regulatory outlook, a long drilling inventory and a developing carbon management business.
Beetaloo Basin acreage, with a price target at a discount to a risked NAV of $60-65/share. Rated Speculative risk.
Free cash flow through the cycle, with a shareholder return policy that currently distributes 75% of FCF.
LNG and offshore oil growth projects (Scarborough, Trion, Louisiana LNG) and a stable dividend payout.
Power generation backlog of 1.75GW, margin expansion and a valuation discount to peers.
Contracted cash flows, capital returns and expansion trains. The price target is below the current price of $330.32.
Compression demand and behind-the-meter power infrastructure growth, with a possible customer agreement as a catalyst.
Power and gas demand growth through Transco expansions and hyperscaler power projects.
Northland Power (NPI-CA, no US listing): offshore wind projects de-risk by late 2026 and the shares trade at a discount to asset value.
Pembina Pipeline (PPL-CA, no US listing): WCSB volume growth and over 80% fee-based EBITDA.
AltaGas (ALA-CA, no US listing): derisking and deleveraging toward its debt/EBITDA target.
PrairieSky Royalty (PSK-CA, no US listing): largest WCSB royalty landowner with Clearwater and Mannville growth.
EDP Renovaveis (EDPR-LIS, no US listing): US renewables upside from higher power prices and improving earnings.

sector_views.rationale: The list holds 17 Outperform names across integrated, E&P, oilfield services, midstream and utilities/renewables, with tight refining and gas demand from power as themes.
US drilling activity is rising and PTEN, Enerflex and Technip Energies were added or kept on the list.
Contracted cash flows and power and gas demand growth support Cheniere, Williams, Kodiak, Pembina and AltaGas.
RBC likes EDP Renovaveis and Northland Power on valuation and de-risking, with US renewables supported by higher power prices.

earnings_insights: PTEN reported mid-single-digit pricing increases in Completion Services in 3Q26, with further upside expected in 2027. RBC estimates 2027 completion gross profit up about 21% y/y to $600MM and 2027 FCF of $444MM (estimates, not reported).
Technip Energies rebased FY26 expectations at 2Q, and RBC expects a gradual margin recovery in 2027. It trades on 6.0x FY27E adj. EV/EBITDA (RBC estimate basis).
BP's refining and trading segment posted its highest quarterly earnings in recent history in 2Q26 (reported). RBC estimates a 2026 average refining margin of $27/bbl vs $13/bbl in 2025.
Northland Power will report Q3/26 results in November 2026 and is expected to give pipeline detail, particularly on battery storage.
Suncor will lift monthly buybacks to $750mm from October 2026, and RBC sees this as sustainable into 2027 (RBC estimate).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Refining is the tightest part of the energy complex, which supports BP's downstream earnings.
Henry Hub is far below Australian domestic gas (about US$9/MMBtu) and JKM (above US$20/MMBtu), which supports Tamboran's regional pricing.
Reports suggest about 45% of Russian capacity is offline, which tightens global refined product supply.

trade_ideas.description: Long Technip Energies (TE-FP), added to the RBC Global Energy Best Ideas List, Outperform, price target EUR 42
trade_ideas.rationale: Record order intake, rebased FY26 estimates and a gradual margin recovery in 2027.
trade_ideas.risk: Macro backdrop tied to the Middle East has dominated the share price.

trade_ideas.description: Long Patterson-UTI Energy (PTEN), added to the RBC Global Energy Best Ideas List, Outperform, price target $17
trade_ideas.rationale: Rising US drilling activity drives margin expansion and FCF conversion, with a valuation below the historical average.

risk_factors: Escalation or a prolonged conflict in the Middle East, which Technip Energies' share price has been tied to. PTEN has minimal exposure.
Demand destruction would loosen the tight refined product market that supports BP's refining margins.
Tamboran carries a Speculative risk rating, with an earlier-stage and higher-risk profile than producing E&Ps.
Kodiak's timing of power equipment delivery depends on signed agreements and customer permits, and compression margins face lube oil cost increases from higher crude prices.
Best Ideas list stop-loss rule removes a stock that is down 20% in the current year or since being added.
geopolitical: Strait of Hormuz closure following the recent Iran/US conflict has limited crude flows and left refined product inventories well below seasonal averages.
Ongoing refining outages in the Middle East and a large share of Russian refining capacity offline are tightening product markets.
A potential Middle East 'peace' deal is hard to predict in timing and structure. Technip Energies expects rebuild work (services first, EPC from 2027+) to follow.
Ovintiv's all-cash acquisition of Logan Energy Corp. was announced on October 26, 2026.
